items.title: Section: Comprehensive Beneficial Conduct — Benefit Now, Benefit Later, and Benefit Spanning Both, Beginning With Honest Livelihood

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切利行？當知此行略有二種。一、未成熟有情能成熟利行；二、已成熟有情令解脫利行。即此利行復由三門。一、於現法利勸導利行；二、於後法利勸導利行；三、於現法後法利勸導利行。於現法利勸導利行者，謂正勸導，以法業德，招集、守護、增長財位，當知是名於現法利勸導利行。由此能令從他獲得廣大名稱及現法樂；由資具樂，攝受安住。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive beneficial conduct? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of two kinds: first, beneficial conduct that matures beings not yet mature; second, beneficial conduct that liberates beings already mature. This same beneficial conduct further unfolds through three approaches: first, guidance towards benefit in this present life; second, guidance towards benefit in future lives; third, guidance towards benefit spanning both this life and lives to come. Guidance towards benefit in this present life means correctly guiding beings, through sound reasoning, genuine effort, and genuine skill, to gather, protect, and increase their own wealth and standing — this is called guidance towards benefit in this present life. Through this, beings come to enjoy a genuinely good reputation among others and genuine ease in this very life, sustained and settled through the ease that comes from having what they genuinely need.

items.title: Section: Encouraging Renunciation for Future Benefit, and Gradual Cultivation Towards Both — Comprehensive Beneficial Conduct Closes

items.zh: 於後法利勸導利行者，謂正勸導棄捨財位，清淨出家，受乞求行以自存活，當知是名於後法利勸導利行。由此能令決定獲得後法安樂，不必獲得現法安樂。於現法後法利勸導利行者，謂正勸導，令在家者、或出家者漸次修行，趣向離欲，當知是名於現法後法利勸導利行。由此能令於現法中，得身輕安、得心輕安，安樂而住；於後法中，或生淨天，或無餘依涅槃界中而般涅槃。
items.en: Guidance towards benefit in future lives means correctly guiding beings to set aside wealth and worldly standing, take up genuine, pure renunciation, and sustain themselves through simple alms — this is called guidance towards benefit in future lives. Through this, beings are assured of genuine ease in lives to come, whether or not they attain ease in this present life. Guidance towards benefit spanning both this life and the next means correctly guiding beings, whether lay or ordained, to gradually and progressively practice, moving towards genuine freedom from craving — this is called guidance towards benefit spanning both this life and the next. Through this, beings attain genuine bodily and mental ease in this very life, dwelling in settled peace; and in the life to come, they are reborn in a genuinely pure heaven, or enter complete liberation within the realm of nirvana without any residue.

items.title: Section: Difficult-Practice Beneficial Conduct — Guiding Those With No Foothold, the Comfortably Careless, and the Firmly Mistaken

items.zh: 云何菩薩難行利行？當知此行略有三種。若諸菩薩，於先未行勝善根因諸有情所，能行利行，是名第一難行利行。何以故？彼諸有情難勸導故。若諸菩薩，於有善因現前執著廣大財位、眾具圓滿諸有情所，能行利行，是名第二難行利行。何以故？彼於廣大極放逸迹、極放逸處耽著轉故。若諸菩薩，於諸外道、著本異道、邪見、邪行諸有情所，能行利行，是名第三難行利行。何以故？彼於自宗愚癡執故，於正法律憎背執故。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's difficult-practice beneficial conduct? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of three kinds. Bodhisattvas who are able to guide beings who have never yet developed any superior wholesome root — this is called the first difficult-practice beneficial conduct. Why is this so? Because such beings are genuinely difficult to guide. Bodhisattvas who are able to guide beings so absorbed in vast wealth and every kind of material fulfilment, already present before them, that genuine carelessness has become their settled state — this is called the second difficult-practice beneficial conduct. Why is this so? Because such beings remain absorbed in the vast places and habits of their own extreme carelessness. Bodhisattvas who are able to guide beings deeply committed to non-Buddhist teachings, holding wrong views and wrong conduct rooted in a rival tradition — this is called the third difficult-practice beneficial conduct. Why is this so? Because such beings are foolishly and firmly attached to their own tradition, and hold a genuine hostility, rooted in that attachment, towards the true teaching and its discipline.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive-Gateway Beneficial Conduct — Building Faith, Discipline, Wisdom, and Generosity Wherever Each Is Missing

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切門利行？當知此行略有四種。謂諸菩薩，不信有情，於信圓滿殷勤勸導，乃至建立；犯戒有情，於戒圓滿殷勤勸導，乃至建立；惡慧有情，於慧圓滿殷勤勸導，乃至建立；慳悋有情，於捨圓滿殷勤勸導，乃至建立。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-gateway beneficial conduct? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of four kinds. Bodhisattvas earnestly guide beings lacking faith towards the genuine fulfilment of faith, all the way to actually establishing it; earnestly guide beings who have broken precepts towards the genuine fulfilment of discipline, all the way to actually establishing it; earnestly guide beings of wrong understanding towards the genuine fulfilment of wisdom, all the way to actually establishing it; and earnestly guide stingy beings towards the genuine fulfilment of generosity, all the way to actually establishing it.

items.title: Section: Virtuous-Person Beneficial Conduct — Five Qualities of Genuinely Skilful Guidance, and Comprehensive-Kind Conduct Opens

items.zh: 云何菩薩善士利行？當知此行略有五種。謂諸菩薩，於真實義勸導有情；於應時宜勸導有情；於能引攝勝妙義利勸導有情；於諸有情柔軟勸導；於諸有情慈心勸導。云何菩薩一切種利行？當知此行，六種、七種，總十三種。云何六種？謂諸菩薩，若諸有情應攝受者，正攝受之；若諸有情應調伏者，正調伏之；若諸有情憎背聖教，除其恚惱；若諸有情處中住者，令入聖教；若諸有情已入聖教，正於三乘令其成熟；若諸有情已成熟者，令得解脫。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's virtuous-person beneficial conduct? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of five kinds: guiding beings grounded in ultimate truth; guiding beings correctly matched to what is timely for them; guiding beings towards genuinely supreme benefit; guiding beings gently; and guiding beings with genuine compassion. What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-kind beneficial conduct? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of thirteen kinds altogether — six of one sort and seven of another. What are the six? Bodhisattvas correctly gather in beings who should be gathered in; correctly tame beings who should be tamed; dispel the hostility of beings who resent and turn away from the sacred teaching; bring beings who remain genuinely undecided into the sacred teaching; correctly mature beings who have already entered the teaching within whichever of the three vehicles suits them; and bring beings who have already matured to genuine liberation.

items.title: Section: Seven More — Guarding the Resources for Practice, and Settling Each Being According to Their Own Path

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，安處一分所化有情，於善資糧守護長養。所謂或依下乘出離，或復依於大乘出離。如令所化於善資糧守護長養，如是或於遠離、或於心一境性、或於清淨諸障、或於修習作意，正安處之。若有聲聞、獨覺種性，即於聲聞、獨覺乘中而正安處；若有如來種姓有情，即於無上正等菩提最上乘中而正安處。
items.en: Bodhisattvas properly settle the portion of beings who can be guided by guarding and nurturing their wholesome resources — whether pursuing liberation through the lesser vehicle or through the great vehicle. Just as bodhisattvas guard and nurture the wholesome resources of those they guide, so too do they properly settle beings in genuine solitude, in one-pointedness of mind, in freedom from meditative obstruction, and in the actual cultivation of mental application. Beings of śrāvaka or solitary-realiser disposition are properly settled within the śrāvaka or solitary-realiser vehicle; beings of the Tathāgata's own disposition are properly settled within the supreme vehicle of supreme, complete awakening.

items.title: Section: Fulfilling-Requests Beneficial Conduct — Untangling the Eight Classical Afflictions That Snare a Practitioner

items.zh: 云何菩薩遂求利行？當知此行略有八種。謂諸菩薩，見諸有情於應慚處為無慚纏之所纏繞，方便開解，令離彼纏。如無慚纏，如是見有於應愧處為無愧纏之所纏繞，若惛沈纏、若睡眠纏、若掉舉纏、若惡作纏、嫉纏、慳纏之所纏繞，方便開解，令離彼纏。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's fulfilling-requests beneficial conduct? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of eight kinds. Bodhisattvas who see beings entangled by shamelessness where genuine shame is warranted skilfully help them understand this and release that entanglement. Just as with shamelessness, so too do bodhisattvas see beings entangled by lack of conscience where genuine conscience is warranted, or entangled by torpor, by drowsiness, by restlessness, by regret, by jealousy, or by stinginess, and skilfully help them understand each and release that entanglement.

blocks.text: How a bodhisattva actually moves people towards the good.
"Maturing beings not yet mature, and liberating those already mature", with benefit in this life, future lives, or both.

For this life: helping beings gain wealth "through lawful work" (Master Cháng Bǎi: obtained by one's own effort). For future lives: guiding them to "set aside wealth and standing, take up pure renunciation". For both: gradual cultivation of calm and insight.

Guiding those who "have never developed any wholesome roots"; the wealthy and careless, attached to their pleasures; and those firmly attached to wrong views. Master Cháng Bǎi: wholesome roots are faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom.
"Guiding the faithless towards faith, precept-breakers towards discipline, those of bad wisdom towards wisdom, the stingy towards generosity." Venerable Miào Jìng: "bad wisdom" means wrong views.
Guiding "by ultimate truth, at the right time, towards supreme benefit, gently, with compassion". Venerable Miào Jìng: even a rebuke is given with compassion.
Settling beings "whether pursuing liberation through the lesser vehicle or the great".
Shamelessness, lack of conscience, torpor, sleep, restlessness, remorse, jealousy, stinginess. Master Cháng Bǎi: in torpor the mind is unclear about its object; in sleep the object is lost.

quiz.q: Comprehensive beneficial conduct is of which two kinds and through which three approaches?
options: maturing the immature, liberating the mature; guidance towards benefit now, later, and both
quiz.why: "Maturing beings not yet mature, and liberating those already mature," through "guidance towards benefit in this life, in future lives, and in both." Venerable Miào Jìng: planting, ripening, liberating — three stages.

quiz.q: Guidance towards present benefit: "through dharma, work, and virtue, gathering and increasing wealth." How do the lectures explain "dharma, work, virtue"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: sound reasoning is "dharma," diligent toil is "work," skill and expertise is "virtue"; Miào Jìng: "dharma" is professional knowledge
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: reasoning in line with correct cause and effect is "dharma"; obtaining wealth through one's own diligent toil is "work"; skill and expertise, not deception, is "virtue." Venerable Miào Jìng: "dharma" means professional knowledge.

quiz.q: Who are the three recipients of difficult beneficial conduct?
options: those without superior wholesome roots; those with good causes but attached to great wealth; outsiders with wrong views
quiz.why: Beings who have never developed superior wholesome roots; beings with good causes but attached to great wealth; outsiders with wrong views and practices. Venerable Miào Jìng: bodhisattvas can do what is hard to do.

quiz.q: The second: "attached to vast traces and places of extreme carelessness." How do the lectures explain "trace" and "place"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: places of amusement are "traces," mansions are "places"; Miào Jìng: "trace" means realm or state
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the places careless people go to amuse themselves are "traces"; "places" are lodgings — mansions and halls that easily make one careless. Venerable Miào Jìng: "trace" means a realm or state.

quiz.q: The English renders "è huì" as "poor understanding." How do the lectures explain it?
options: "bad wisdom" means wrong knowledge and wrong views; "poor understanding" is too mild
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: beings of "bad wisdom" are those with wrong knowledge and views. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise. The English "poor understanding" understates it.

quiz.q: What are the five good-person beneficial conducts?
options: guiding by ultimate truth, by timeliness, towards supreme benefit, gently, and with compassion
quiz.why: Guiding beings by ultimate truth, by what is timely, towards supreme benefit, gently, and with compassion. Venerable Miào Jìng: one rebukes, but gently, so it is easier to accept.

quiz.q: Fulfilling-requests beneficial conduct untangles which eight entanglements?
options: shamelessness, lack of conscience, torpor, sleep, restlessness, remorse, jealousy, stinginess
quiz.why: Shamelessness, lack of conscience, torpor, sleep, restlessness, remorse, jealousy, and stinginess. Master Cháng Bǎi: jealousy is countered by teaching the merit of rejoicing.
